Index116BWhen a teacher wants to search by the name of a student, the DBMS needs to go through the table row by row. In the worst case, if the teacher wants to find a student named Guy, it needs to go through 11 records, i.e. the whole table, to find the required record.

Index117BSince the name of a student, i.e. NAME, is expected to be searched frequently, we can index that field to speed up the data retrieval process.Indexing NAME creates an index table containing the indexed field and a pointer to the related records only.

Index118BThe data in the indexed field of the index table is sorted in alphabetic order (or ascending order if it is a number field). The sorting allows the DBMS to perform binary search.The record in the middle, i.e. the 6th one, Finn is checked.It starts with an F, which is before G as in Guy.Therefore, every record before the 6th one cannot be our guy.
Index119BThe record in the middle of the rest, i.e. the 9th one, Hans is checked. It starts with an H, which is after G as in Guy. Therefore, every record after the 9th one cannot be our guy.
LEFT JOIN12BThe following SQL statement lists the student identity code, the student name, class, the club name and the club room of every student who gets at least 60 scores.

Index120BThe record in the middle of the rest, i.e. the 7th one, Gabe is checked. It starts with an Ga, which is before Gu as in Guy. Therefore, every record before the 7th one cannot be our guy (though every single one of them is already eliminated).
Index121BThe record in the middle of the rest, i.e. the 8th one, Guy is checked. To our surprise, this is the guy

Index122BAs shown in the previous example, we can see how indexing speeds up the data retrieval process.In the worst case, the DBMS only needs to go through 4 records, instead of 11 records, i.e. the whole table, to find the required record.However, the index table needs to be updated when:the data in the indexed field changes (e.g. the name of the student Guy is changed to Gal); ora new record is added (e.g. a new student named Hope is added).
Index123BSince the names Gal and Hope is not in the index table, it fails to search for them if it is not updated.
Index124BTo index a field of a table, we may use the keyword CREATE INDEX.Normally, the name of the index is used only when we have to drop the index.
Index125BTo drop an index, we may use the following SQL statement.If we forget the name of the index, we may find it out by using SHOW CREATE TABLE.

View98A1. List the name of each student taught by Mr Suen and has a final score below 60.We have to join STUDENT with CLASS to see if a student is taught by Mr Suen.SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT s, CLASS cl WHERE s.CLASS = cl.CLASS AND	TEACH = 'Mr Suen' AND SCORE1 * 0.4 + SCORE2 * 0.6 < 60

VIEW99A2. List the name of each student who joins at least two clubs and has a final score above 60.We have to count the number of clubs joined by each student in a subquery.SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE SCORE1 * 0.4 + SCORE2 * 0.6 > 60 AND 	SID IN (SELECT SID FROM SC GROUP BY SID HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2)
